groups.spec_text: parallel sentence pairs; add <SOS>/<EOS>; build subword tokenizers per language (or a shared one); pad + attention masks

items.evidence: 58,000 English-Odia candidate pairs were streamed from the ai4bharat/samanantar 'or' config and saved to data/raw/candidates.parquet; after MAX_LEN=64 subword filtering 40,000 pairs were seed-shuffled (RANDOM_SEED=42) into on-disk splits of 36,000 train / 2,000 val / 2,000 test.

Each tokenizer carries a TemplateProcessing post-processor with template '<SOS> $A <EOS>', so every encode() call is wrapped automatically; encoding a sample English string returns ids beginning with 1 (<SOS>) and ending with 2 (<EOS>).

Two independent byte-level BPE tokenizers were trained and saved, tokenizers/en_bpe.json and tokenizers/or_bpe.json, each with a verified vocabulary size of exactly 8,000 tokens and identical special-token ids <PAD>=0, <SOS>=1, <EOS>=2, <UNK>=3 (asserted at training time).
collate_fn right-pads each batch to that batch's longest sequence with PAD_ID=0 via _pad_batch, for both the source and target side, and returns the padded id tensors used by the training loop.

Three mask builders exist and are wired into every forward pass: make_padding_mask for encoder self-attention, make_decoder_self_attn_mask (causal AND pad, shape [B,1,T,T]) for decoder self-attention, and make_cross_attn_mask ([B,1,1,S]) for cross-attention; masks are boolean True='attend' and are applied via masked_fill(~mask, -1e9) before softmax.

items.requirement: No sentence leakage between train / val / test
items.evidence: split.py drops duplicate source sentences and then asserts pairwise-empty intersections between the train, val and test source-sentence sets before any parquet is written, so an examiner cannot find the same English sentence in two splits.

groups.spec_text: Build exactly section 5.6: embedding + positional encoding -> N encoder blocks (self-attn -> FFN, residual+LN) -> N decoder blocks (masked self-attn -> cross-attn -> FFN) -> linear+softmax. Start small: d=128, heads=4, N=2 - it must fit class compute.

items.evidence: Embeddings composes TokenEmbedding (nn.Embedding scaled by sqrt(d_model)=sqrt(128)) with a fixed sinusoidal PositionalEncoding built from the sin/cos 10000^(2i/d) formula and registered as a non-persistent buffer of length MAX_LEN+16 = 80; both encoder and decoder use it.

items.requirement: N encoder blocks: self-attn -> FFN, residual + LayerNorm
items.evidence: EncoderBlock.forward is exactly x = norm1(x + dropout1(self_attn(x,x,x,src_mask))) then x = norm2(x + dropout2(feed_forward(x))) -- post-norm residual as in Vaswani et al.; Encoder stacks N_ENCODER_LAYERS=2 such blocks in an nn.ModuleList.

items.requirement: N decoder blocks: masked self-attn -> cross-attn -> FFN
items.evidence: DecoderBlock.forward runs masked self-attention (tgt_mask = causal AND pad), then cross-attention with the encoder output as key/value under the source pad mask, then the FFN, each wrapped in its own residual + LayerNorm (norm1/norm2/norm3); Decoder stacks N_DECODER_LAYERS=2 such blocks.

Seq2SeqTransformer ends in a separate nn.Linear(128, tgt_vocab_size=8000) output projection returning raw logits (untied from the target embedding by default, TIE_OUTPUT_PROJECTION=False); softmax is applied by nn.CrossEntropyLoss at training time and by F.log_softmax at beam-search decode time, and tests/test_model_shapes.py::test_forward_returns_raw_logits_not_probabilities pins this contract.

items.requirement: Exact required hyperparameters d=128, heads=4, N=2
items.evidence: configs/base.py sets D_MODEL=128, N_HEADS=4, N_ENCODER_LAYERS=2, N_DECODER_LAYERS=2 (with D_FF=512, DROPOUT=0.1) and these are the constructor defaults for every module, so the built model matches the spec exactly with no override path used in training or evaluation.

Instantiating the real model against the two 8k tokenizers gives 4,005,696 parameters (all trainable), and the full 36,000-pair training run completed on a Kaggle CPU at about 410 s/epoch (~2 hours for 18 epochs) at batch size 128 -- no GPU required.

items.requirement: Attention implemented from scratch (not a torch built-in)
items.evidence: MultiHeadAttention hand-rolls q/k/v/out nn.Linear projections, head splitting/merging, QK^T/sqrt(head_dim) scoring, masking and softmax; grepping src/ finds no use of nn.Transformer, nn.MultiheadAttention, nn.TransformerEncoder or F.scaled_dot_product_attention (the only hit is a comment in dataset.py).

groups.spec_text: Train: teacher forcing, cross-entropy ignoring pad tokens, Adam with warmup; watch for the causal mask bug (if val loss is suspiciously perfect, your decoder is peeking!).

items.evidence: run_epoch feeds the gold target shifted right as decoder input and scores against the gold target shifted left: decoder_input = tgt_ids[:, :-1], decoder_target = tgt_ids[:, 1:].

The loss is nn.CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=PAD_ID, label_smoothing=0.1) with PAD_ID=0, and reported epoch loss is renormalized by the non-pad token count ((decoder_target != PAD_ID).sum()) so padding influences neither the gradient nor the logged number.

torch.optim.Adam(lr=1.0, betas=(0.9, 0.98), eps=1e-9) is driven by a Noam LambdaLR schedule, lr = d_model^-0.5 * min(step^-0.5, step * warmup^-1.5) with WARMUP_STEPS=900, stepped once per batch; gradients are clipped to norm 1.0.

Beyond simply watching the loss curve, tests/test_masks.py contains four passing tests: a full-model leak-invariance test (logits at positions <= t are identical when target tokens after t are changed), a negative control that reruns the same check through a deliberately all-True mask and asserts it FAILS -- proving the invariance test is not vacuous -- plus position-by-position assertions that future keys and <PAD> keys are always blocked and valid causal keys never are.

items.requirement: Real training run completed, loss behaves correctly
items.evidence: reports/training_history.json records 18 epochs on the full 36,000-pair train split with train loss 5.0468 -> 1.7868 and val loss 3.2268 -> 1.9257, decreasing together with validation consistently above training and no discontinuous drop -- the opposite of the 'suspiciously perfect' leakage symptom the spec warns about.

groups.spec_text: Inference: greedy decode loop (feed outputs back until <EOS>); beam search = bonus marks.

items.requirement: Greedy decode loop feeding outputs back until <EOS>
items.evidence: greedy_decode starts from a [[<SOS>]] tensor, repeatedly runs the full model, takes argmax over the last position, concatenates it onto the running target and breaks as soon as the emitted id equals EOS_ID=2, capped at GREEDY_MAX_DECODE_LEN=64; it is the decoder used for the reported BLEU over all 2,000 test pairs.

beam_search_decode implements a full beam with BEAM_WIDTH=4 and length-normalized scoring (cum_logprob / length^0.6, BEAM_LENGTH_PENALTY=0.6), completed-hypothesis collection and early stopping; run against the real kaggle_run_best.pt checkpoint on 'There is nothing on the ground.' it returns a different, more complete hypothesis than greedy (beam 'ସେଠାରେ କିଛି ନାହିଁ।' vs greedy 'କିଛି ବି ନାହିଁ।'), and it is exposed in the dashboard's translate path.

Not asked for by the spec: both decoders bar any token that would complete an already-seen n-gram of size NO_REPEAT_NGRAM_SIZE=3, a standard inference-time fix for the degenerate repetition loops small greedy models fall into; four tests in tests/test_repetition.py pin the banned-token logic and assert a random model never repeats a 3-gram under greedy decoding.

groups.spec_text: Evaluate: BLEU score (n-gram overlap with reference translation) + show 5 sample translations, including one long sentence to discuss limitations.

items.evidence: sacrebleu corpus BLEU over the full 2,000-pair test split is 2.19 (precisions 19.1/4.0/1.2/0.4, BP 0.885, hyp_len 13,648 vs ref_len 15,317), with identical postprocessing -- decode, strip special tokens, normalize whitespace -- applied to hypotheses and references alike; decoding all 2,000 examples took 340.4 s.

reports/eval_results.json contains a 'samples' array of exactly 5 entries, each with source, reference and hypothesis, and the same 5 rows are reproduced as a table in the write-up; NUM_SAMPLE_TRANSLATIONS=5 in the config drives select_samples.

items.requirement: One long sentence among the samples
items.evidence: select_samples deterministically reserves the 5th slot for a source sentence at or above the 90th percentile of test-split source word length (LONG_SENTENCE_PERCENTILE=0.90), drawing the other 4 from the remainder; the selected long example is 'BJP media cell head and Rajya Sabha member Anil Baluni dismissed the charge.' (12 English words).

The write-up diagnoses the long-sentence failure as degenerate repetition and names its two causes (d=128 / 2 decoder layers of capacity, and a 36k-pair training set), and it is backed by a full-test-set measurement rather than one anecdote: reports/length_quality_analysis.json scores all 2,000 examples and shows mean sentence BLEU falling 9.726 -> 6.959 -> 5.472 -> 4.747 -> 2.891 across the 3-5 / 6-8 / 9-11 / 12-15 / 16-20 word buckets while the repetition rate climbs 17.75% -> 72.6% (Pearson r = -0.2412 vs source word length, -0.2676 vs subword length).

groups.spec_text: use a Unicode-clean corpus (e.g., Samanantar / OPUS pairs), normalize Odia Unicode, and expect subword tokenization to matter a lot for a morphologically rich Indic language - mention this in your write-up for extra credit

items.evidence: The corpus is ai4bharat/samanantar, config 'or' -- one of the two sources the spec names explicitly -- loaded in streaming mode with per-example cleaning and source-side deduplication before any pair is kept.

clean_text applies Unicode NFC normalization, then strips ZWSP and BOM outright, removes ZWJ/ZWNJ runs at string edges and collapses interior runs of 2+ joiners to a single one -- deliberately preserving a lone ZWJ/ZWNJ because it carries meaning in Indic conjunct formation -- then normalizes whitespace; an added inspect_nfc_anomalies() idempotency audit over 500 Odia samples found 0 anomalies.

items.requirement: Subword tokenization discussion for a morphologically rich Indic language
items.evidence: The write-up devotes a dedicated section to it with measured, not asserted, numbers: at the same 8k vocabulary the pilot found English averaging 17.5 subword tokens (median 13) against 49.8 for Odia (median 39), which is why MAX_LEN=64 drops ~22-23% of pairs almost always on the Odia side; the section further covers multi-byte script encoding cost, suffixation-heavy morphology consuming BPE merge budget, and conjunct/virama normalization, plus the measured retention curve at MAX_LEN 32/48/64/80/96/128.
